svg.title: One Game of Life generation split across three workers
svg.desc: A schematic row map shows a 12-row world split into three horizontal strips. Worker 1 owns rows 0 through 3 and receives ghost rows 11 and 4. Worker 2 owns rows 4 through 7 and receives ghost rows 3 and 8. Worker 3 owns rows 8 through 11 and receives ghost rows 7 and 0. The broker copies both ghost rows from the current generation, including wraparound at the top and bottom. Each worker computes and returns only its four owned rows; workers do not exchange rows with one another. The broker places results into their original row ranges as replies arrive, waits for every worker, then publishes the next world. Left and right columns also wrap during neighbor lookup. Cell states are omitted to emphasize row ownership and data movement.
svg.text: The broker sends each worker four owned rows plus two ghost rows for neighbor context.
Example: 12 rows · 3 workers · 6 input rows and 4 output rows per worker
